title: Data Subject Request Playbook — inference outputs & LLM explanations
body:
Purpose:
This playbook defines Redwood's internal process for responding to data subject requests (access, deletion, portability) that concern inference outputs, LLM explanations, and any artifacts derived from user queries (including cached prefixes, KV cache snapshots, and telemetry). It is intended for security, legal, product, SRE, and support teams.

Scope: what counts as 'inference output' for DSARs: 
- Model generation tokens returned to a user (text, structured JSON, function-call payloads)
- Any persisted chat history or session transcripts stored in our databases or object storage
- Cached prefixes or KV cache entries persisted beyond ephemeral runtime that could reproduce user output
- Aggregated telemetry or logs that include de-identified but re-identifiable fragments (e.g. unique internal trace ids tied to user accounts)
- Human annotations, safety-review notes, or post-process edits stored by the moderation/quality team

High-level SLAs and roles: 
- Legal: owns final determination on scope, exemptions, and legal hold triggers (24h initial review).
- Security & Compliance: executes technical evidence collection, cache queries, and purge scripts (SRE assist) (48h).
- Support/CS: primary contact with requester; issues templated responses and tracks consent where needed (72h for acknowledgement, 30 calendar days for full response unless law requires otherwise).
- Product/Model Ops: advises on model-state questions, model variant behavior, and rollback options.

Initial intake checklist (support):
1) Verify identity using standard ID process; log verification artifact ID to case.
2) Create incident ticket JIRA/DSAR reference and tag with 'dsar-inference'.
3) Capture request type (access, delete, portability) and any identifiers (user id, session id, approximate timestamps, model id if known).
4) If request includes third-party data or law enforcement language, escalate to Legal immediately.

Technical triage (security & SRE):
- Step A: Locate candidate artifacts
  - Query session storage for session_id/user_id windows +/- 1 hour.
  - Search object store (s3) for transcripts and attachments by metadata tags (user-id, api-key).
  - Run KV-cache-scan restricted script (see linked_artifacts) to surface any persisted KV dumps referencing the requester.
  - Check persistent prefix cache buckets and any disk-backed batch caches on serving nodes.
- Step B: Evaluate re-identification risk
  - If stored artifact is full text and maps directly to user account, mark as 'direct'.
  - If artifact is aggregate or hashed, attempt controlled re-hydration in a safe environment (Legal approval required).
- Step C: Evidence capture
  - Create a signed, time-stamped snapshot of located artifacts (hash + storage location) and store in evidence bucket with strict ACLs.
  - Record which services/hosts produced the output and kernel selection (model_variant/quantization).

Purge / remediations (deletion requests):
- If artifact is under our control (object storage, DB row): schedule deletion job with unique purge-id; perform secure deletion for hot storage and logical deletion for backups where appropriate.
- KV cache purges: run atomic purge for keyspace related to user account; verify with test query in non-prod mirror to confirm expired output cannot be re-produced.
- Ephemeral/transient caches (in-memory): document that these expired by TTL; include evidence of TTL config and timing when responding.
- Backups & replication: flag backup retention windows; if deletion cannot be guaranteed in a live window, issue interim statement to requester and provide estimated completion + remediation plan.

Access requests (portability / disclosure):
- Provide a packaged export containing transcripts, model outputs, timestamps, and metadata fields (model id, model version, region) unless redaction is required.
- Redaction guidance: remove internal-only debug fields, trace IDs that identify other customers, and any PII belonging to other accounts.
- For large exports (multi-GB): coordinate with requester for secure transfer (GPG or secure bucket link with one-time token).

Communication templates (support) — acknowledgement (short):
"Thanks — we received your request regarding inference records. We will respond within 30 calendar days. If we need more time or additional verification, we will contact you. Reference: [JIRA-ID]."

Communication template — substantive response (delete confirmation):
"We completed our review and have removed the listed inference artifacts associated with your account. Items removed: session transcripts, object-store blobs, and cache entries. Proof of deletion: [purge-id, S3-delete-logs-hash]. If you have further concerns, reply referencing [JIRA-ID]."

Legal hold & preservation triggers:
- If a DSAR is part of litigation or investigation, Legal will immediately issue a legal hold and freeze relevant deletion jobs. Do not run purge until legal hold is lifted.
- Logging: capture host-level forensic logs and preserve chain-of-custody for evidence. Use the 'forensics-preserve' playbook for snapshotting node disks.

Special considerations for model explanations and provenance requests:
- Explanation artifacts (WHY did model produce this) may require: prompt chain, system messages, model variant, sampling seed, and KV prefix contents. Some items (sampling seed) are considered internal and may be redacted unless court order demands disclosure — escalate to Legal.
- If requester seeks reproduction (portability that reproduces output), we must evaluate whether reproduction would disclose other customers' data via shared caches or model updates. Product to advise on 'safe reproduction' procedures (non-prod mirror, syntheticized prompt mapping).

Risk & mitigations (quick notes):
- Risk: Persistent prefix caching can leak prior user tokens as context. Mitigation: enforce TTLs, rotate sharded cache namespaces per-account, minimize persistent write-to-disk of prefixes.
- Risk: Aggregated telemetry may be re-identifiable. Mitigation: add stronger sampling, remove exact timestamps for DSAR exports, or add controlled re-identification workflow.

Unresolved decisions / open questions (for Legal + Product):
- Should sampling seeds used during generation be treated as internal debug data exempt from normal DSAR exports? (Legal to decide)
- Policy on retention of ephemeral KV snapshots for SLO debugging vs DSAR rights — conservative default is to treat them as potentially subject to deletion unless escrowed for compliance reasons.

Appendix A: quick command snippets (for security ops) — (internal only):
- s3 find: aws s3api list-objects --bucket redwood-inference-transcripts --query "Contents[?contains(Key, 'user-1234')].Key"
- kv purge: python scripts/kv_purge.py --namespace=shard-17 --user="user-1234" --dry-run
- evidence hash: sha256sum /evidence/snapshot-20260308.json > snapshot-20260308.sha256

Appendix B: DSAR response checklist (tick-box style):
- [ ] Identity verified
- [ ] Ticket created and linked to Legal
- [ ] Candidate artifacts located and hashed
- [ ] Evidence snapshots stored (read-only ACL)
- [ ] Purge job scheduled OR export prepared
- [ ] Communication sent to requester
- [ ] Legal hold checked (cleared or active)

Notes to reviewers: this is a working draft. Need Legal sign-off on explanation redaction rules, and Product to confirm KV cache retention and TTL engineering plan. Also want a small tabletop exercise with SRE + Support to run a mock DSAR that includes a model explanation request (simulate secrets/redaction edge cases).

Last internal edits: 2026-03-10 by Aisha Patel — updated technical triage steps and evidence storage naming conventions.
summary: Working DSAR playbook for inference outputs and LLM explanation requests. Draft — legal review needed. Includes intake, technical triage, purge/export steps, communications templates, and unresolved questions.
